raw: {"analysis":"Response HWH provides a more operationally complete plan, correctly addressing the zero-downtime requirement for the main release branch (which HND conflates with the merge strategy) and explicitly sequencing the Security Lead gate as post-merge pre-deployment. HWH also properly accounts for the $45/22-minute cost constraint by limiting test runs and doing local sanity checks first, whereas HND doesn't address cost optimization. However, HWH contains a factual error in Lane 4, stating the image is shared across four products when the repository facts say three other products (four total). HND makes the same error in Lane C. Both handle the flaky Tuesday check correctly, but HND's reviewer strategy (requiring someone outside Platform Trust) is unnecessarily restrictive given the repo is managed by that team. HWH's rollback plan is more thorough, explicitly documenting the old image cache and the 4-hour window constraint, while HND's is adequate but less detailed.","verdict":"HWH"}
